text:
IncidentBot: 🚨 Incident opened: serving-runtime OOM spikes observed across several GPU nodes in prod-west1. Suspected root: KV cache / paged-attention allocator fragmentation causing slow memory creep. Priority: P1. Paging @oncall.

Maria K: ack — I'm on it, switching to incident mode.

Sunil P: saw spikes at 15:12 UTC, margin was tiny before OOMs started. Heap and GPU memory climb steadily over hours.

Kevin L: any crashloop pods? which node pools?

Maria K: node-pool: gpu-a, gpu-b. 3 containers per node in affected pool. yes a few container restarts and one node marked NotReady due to CUDA driver errors right after OOMs.

Emily R: customer impact: a handful of mid-tier customers saw 502/503s; partial degraded throughput for chat endpoints. No data leak. Notified CS to pause new signups for affected tenants.

Sunil P: posting recent memory trend snapshot and tail of runtime logs.

```# mem trend (samples)
2026-03-14T14:00 gpu_mem=12GB kv_cache=1.1GB allocator_free=200MB
2026-03-14T16:00 gpu_mem=13GB kv_cache=1.4GB allocator_free=160MB
2026-03-14T18:00 gpu_mem=14.2GB kv_cache=1.9GB allocator_free=80MB
2026-03-14T20:10 gpu_mem=15.8GB kv_cache=2.3GB allocator_free=12MB
```

```# last lines from runtime.log
2026-03-14T20:09:58 ERROR serving: CUDA out of memory when allocating stream KVChunk
2026-03-14T20:09:59 WARN allocator: fragmentation: free_list_blocks=14 small_fragments=5320
2026-03-14T20:10:01 INFO container: restarting due to OOM
```

Maria K: looks like paged-attention allocator isn't releasing freed pages, fragmentation slowly increasing. Could be free-list metadata leak.

Kevin L: can we evict KV cache prefix for affected models as short-term mitigation?

Sunil P: yes -- we have runtime flags to disable KV caching per model. Propose: 1) disable kv_cache for Llama-2-large canary 2) trigger rolling restart of 2 pods in pool gpu-a 3) ramp traffic back then observe.

Emily R: recommend communicating to impacted customers: degraded throughput, retries in effect, ETA for mitigation 30–45m. I can draft message after confirmation.

devops-bot: @infra scheduled rolling-restart job job-rr-1719001234 for pool gpu-a (2 pods) — ETA 5m.

Maria K: implementing kv_cache disable on canary now. Command: ``curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/configs -d '{"model":"llama-2-large","kv_cache":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'``

Sunil P: can confirm immediate memory slope decrease on canary after disabling. Patch shows allocator_free recovering slowly.

Kevin L: good. queue a patch for allocator free-list accounting. Any repro?

Maria K: repro steps on dev: load a long-running chat session with paged-attention and repeatedly allocate/deallocate large KV prefixes. After ~12h we saw same slow creep. attaching small test harness snippet.

```# repro harness
for i in range(0,10000):
  model.alloc_kv(prefix=f"p{i}", size=1<<26)
  model.free_kv(prefix=f"p{i}")
  sleep(0.5)
```

Sunil P: root cause hypothesis: free() path fails to return all pages to buddy allocator when paged-attention fragmentation threshold crossed. Leaked page descriptors accumulate in allocator internal vector. Need a fix: ensure pages are returned to GPU driver allocator and clear descriptor vector on eviction.

Kevin L: short-term: aggressive KV eviction policy + restart cadence for affected pools. Medium-term: hotspot patch to allocator (pull request in review), plus add more metrics: "allocator_live_descriptors" & "kv_fragmentation_ratio".

IncidentBot: Incident timeline updated: mitigation started at 1719002100, partial recovery observed 1719003600.

Maria K: rolling restarts finished for 2 pods. canary shows stable GPU mem + no OOMs for 20m. proceeding to restart remaining pods in gpu-a with 1m gap.

Emily R: CS notified customers A, B, C (who had >10% error rate). Draft sent.

Sunil P: prepping hotfix branch: allocator:ensure_free_return + unit tests for descriptor leak. Will push in 20m.

Kevin L: we should also add an emergency KILL on per-container memory > 95% to avoid node-wide driver failure. Will open infra ticket.

Maria K: live mitigation checklist (done/in-progress):
- [x] disable kv_cache for culprit models (canary)
- [x] rolling restarts (2/2 canary pods)
- [x] dashboard alerts tuned for fragmentation ratio
- [ ] roll restarts across gpu-a (in progress)

Sunil P: hotfix PR opened: https://git.redwood/inference/runtime/pulls/542 (allocator: ensure_free_return). Requesting speedy review.

Maria K: testing hotfix in staging with long-run harness. initial run 6h looks promising (no leak).

Emily R: customer comms going out now: "We identified a memory fragmentation issue leading to transient outages. We're mitigating and rolling a fix. No data loss. We'll follow up with RCA."

Kevin L: post-incident action items:
- telemetry: add "allocator_live_descriptors" and fragmentation metrics (owner: Sunil)
- code: land allocator free_list fix + add integration test (owner: Sunil/Kevin)
- infra: implement per-container mem guard and faster node draining (owner: Kevin)
- runbook: update paged-attention OOM mitigation steps (owner: Maria)

Maria K: handing off to @Sunil for final patch and full roll. I'm going offline in 25m but will be reachable for critical escalations.

Sunil P: taking over. Will coordinate full rollout and postmortem. Current status: degradation mitigated, can proceed to apply hotfix to prod after 30m of steady signals.

IncidentBot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident closed after postmortem to be scheduled.

Kevin L: thanks everyone — great fast work. I'll prepare the postmortem template and initial timeline.

Emily R: adding note: CS will follow-up with impacted customers with a timeline for the fix and any credits.

Sunil P: logging this for postmortem: suspected bug id: ALLOC-1973. Will include memory graphs, logs, and the repro harness.

Maria K: good job team. :thumbsup:
